instruction: Set up autossh as a systemd service for a reverse tunnel
output:
<think>
The user wants to perform a service management operation using sudo.

`sudo` is the appropriate choice — sudo command execution and management.
`systemctl` will be used for manage systemd services and units.
Key flags: `-R` (recursive operation) — chosen to match the exact requirement.

Before executing: SERVICE CONSIDERATION: Restart services during maintenance windows. Check unit dependencies beforehand with `systemctl list-dependencies`. PRIVILEGE ESCALATION: Running with `sudo` — double-check the command for typos or path mistakes before pressing Enter.
</think>
sudo cat > /etc/systemd/system/autossh-tunnel.service << 'EOF'
[Unit]
Description=AutoSSH tunnel to remote
After=network.target

[Service]
Environment="AUTOSSH_GATETIME=0"
ExecStart=/usr/bin/autossh -M 0 -o ServerAliveInterval=30 -o ServerAliveCountMax=3 -NT -R 2222:localhost:22 user@remote.example.com
Restart=always
RestartSec=10
User=autossh

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
EOF
sudo systemctl daemon-reload && sudo systemctl enable --now autossh-tunnel.service
